title: Reimagining Food Innovation
summary: Some of the most significant innovations surrounding food are not high-tech scientific advances but low-tech social practices and relations, such as new ways of cooperating and distributing responsibility. To fix our broken food systems, we must demand that the best of these practices receive respect and investment.

title: Gun Buybacks Work, But Not the Way We Thought
summary: Some argue that gun buybacks are pointless unless they lower homicide rates. But new research into Mexico City’s gun-buyback program suggests that such measures can meaningfully reduce nonlethal injuries, which are more common than homicides, and can have serious psychological and other lasting health consequences.

title: Can the AI Mineral Rush Advance a Just Green Transition?
summary: The scramble to secure huge amounts of copper, aluminum, lithium, cobalt, and other minerals for AI infrastructure risks undoing the progress made, as part of the green transition, toward more responsible mining practices. But it could also be an opportunity to support sustainable development in producer countries.
